title: NAILS config --json
description: Machine-readable config envelope (contract version 2): one document for `config path`, `config show`, `config validate`, `config set` or `config unset`. The data shape differs by subcommand (path/exists, the effective configuration with the source of each top-level key and of each key of a table, written table.key, path/valid, or for set and unset the file, whether it was written and each key's value before and after), so data is validated only as an object, except the data of set and unset, which is strict; the envelope frame and the error body are strict. `config show --example --json` is a usage error, and so is a key or a value set or unset does not take (exit 2). Set and unset refuse a file that is not on the volume nails runs from, a link or another filesystem on the way to it, a volume with no NAILS layout and, while a hidden session runs, is entering or was left behind by an interrupted entry, a change that points the hidden volume root or the state file away from where the session recorded them (exit 4); a file that cannot be read or would not be valid is the error `config` (exit 3); a write that failed is exit 1. A Ctrl+C or SIGTERM before the result (for set and unset, before the new file replaced the old one; after that the change is reported as made) is the shared cancel shape: the error `cancelled`, no data, exit 130. An internal error is the error `internal_error`, exit 1.

data.description: The data of `config set` and `config unset`.

path.description: The file that was changed, or that would have been.

written.description: Whether the file was written: false when every key already held what was asked.

changes.description: One entry per key named, in the order given.

key.description: The key, as docs/configuration.md lists it.

before.description: The value the file held, as JSON; null where the file did not set the key.

after.description: The value the file holds; null where it no longer sets the key, so its default applies.
